ai.description: *Cnemaspis ajijae* is a small gecko reaching 35 mm SVL. It features a dark brown dorsum with yellow-spotted flanks and a distinct, pale yellow vertebral stripe. A diagnostic black spot marks the throat.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis ajijae* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, spine-like tubercles along the flanks, absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis ajijae* is endemic to the Western Ghats, typically inhabiting moist deciduous forests and rocky outcrops at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Cnemaspis ajijae is a nocturnal gecko that remains active at night, foraging for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis ajijae* is oviparous, laying a single, hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity observed during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis ajijae* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, where it inhabits rocky outcrops at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
